(O&M) Satpal vs Shanti Devi on 12 July, 2024
 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:087051
 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana
At Chandigarh

(315)
 Crr No. 2440 of 2006
 Date of Decision: 12.07.2024
Satpal
 ...Petitioner
 Vs
Shanti Devi
 ...Respondent
Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vikram Aggarwal
Present: None for the petitioner.
Mr. Athar Ahmed, D.A.G. Punjab.

** * *
Vikram Aggarwal, J (Oral)

The present revision petition assails the judgment dated 18.11.2006, passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Bathinda, vide which appeal against the judgment of conviction dated 01.03.2006 convicting the petitioner under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC')
and order of sentence dated 04.03.2006 sentencing the petitioner to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years and to pay a fine of `5000/- was dismissed.
2.
The respondent-complainant-Shanti Devi and the petitioner- accused were issues of one late Bishan Dass, who had expired on 13.04.1991.
He was the owner of two residential houses situated at Rama Mandi.

The allegation was that the present petitioner-accused along with Phul Chand and Laxmi Devi who were also the issues of Bhisan Dass executed a registered General Power of Attorney (for short 'GPA') in favour of the respondent-complainant on 11.12.1995.
Accordingly, the respondent- 1 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:087051 complainant had rented the residential houses owned by Bishan Dass to Om Parkash and Sri Ram for a period of five years.
The allegation was that the accused namely Satpal, Phul Chand and Laxmi Devi had dispossessed Om Parkash forcibly and illegally on 15.10.1999.
The petitioner-accused got the house transferred in his name in the (O&M) Satpal vs Shanti Devi on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42347876/
1 Municipal record and thereafter alienated the same.
3. A complaint was submitted to the police, but on no action having been taken, a private complaint was instituted.
The petitioner- accused was summoned under Section 420 IPC vide order dated 07.06.2000.

After pre-charge evidence having been led, charge under Section 420 IPC was framed on 18.12.2004.
4.
Four witnesses namely CW-1-Shanti Devi, CW-3-Om Parkash, CW-4-Ram Kishan and CWP-5-Sarla Devi, were cross-examined after the framing of charges.
Thereafter, the complainant closed the after-charge evidence and statement of accused was recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

In defence, one witness namely Jagtar Singh was produced as DW-1.
5.

After considering the evidence led by the parties, the Court of the Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Talwandi Sabo, convicted the accused under Section 420 IPC vide judgment of conviction dated 01.03.2006.
Vide order of sentence dated 04.03.2006, the petitioner-accused was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years.
A fine of `5000/- was also imposed and in default of payment of the said fine, the petitioner-accused was ordered to further undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of three months.
2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:087051 6.

The appeal against the said judgment of conviction and order of sentence was dismissed by the Court of the Additional Sessions Judge, Bathinda, vide judgment dated 18.11.2006 leading to filing of the present revision petition but sentence of 02 years was modified to 06 months.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. No one has appeared on behalf of the parties.

8. As the matter pertains to the year 2006 and a perusal of the orders passed from time to time show that learned counsel appearing on behalf of the parties had been making requests for adjournment, I deem it appropriate not to adjourn the case any further.

It was held by the Supreme Court of India in the case of Surya Baksh Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, 2014(14) SCC 222, that where in a criminal case/appeal, the counsel for the appellant or the appellant himself does not appear, the High Court was not bound to appoint an amicus curiae and could very well decide the appeal on merits after carefully examining the same.

entities.text: Surya Baksh Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, 2014(14) SCC 222
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. On a perusal of the judgments passed by the Courts below, this Court is of the considered opinion that there is no error or illegality in the same warranting any interference.
Both the Courts below have elaborately discussed the evidence led by the parties and have concurrently found that the petitioner-accused had committed the offence punishable under Section 420 IPC.
The evidence given by all four witnesses examined by the complainant was discussed in detail and due reference was also given to the law on the subject.
It was found that it was a clear case of cheating and the accused was, therefore, convicted under Section 420 IPC and sentenced in the manner referred to in the preceding paragraphs.
The judgments, as noticed earlier do not, therefore, warrant any interference in so far as the 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:087051

issue of conviction is (O&M) Satpal vs Shanti Devi on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42347876/
2 concerned.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the judgments as regards the conviction of the petitioner under Section 420 IPC are upheld.
10. Coming to the issue of sentence, I have given my thoughtful consideration to the same.
The complaint was filed in the year 1999 and conviction was recorded by the Court of SDJM, Talwandi Sabo on 01.03.2006.
Even, the First Appellate Court decided the appeal on 18.11.2006 and since 2006, the present revision petition is pending before this Court.
As per the custody certificate, the petitioner-accused has undergone sentence of three months and 2 days.
More than 25 years have gone by.
The petitioner-accused has undergone a protracted trial and has suffered the agony of the same for the last 25 years.

Still further, as has been observed, out of the reduced sentence of six months, he has already undergone more than three months and, therefore, under the circumstances,
the present case is a fit case where the sentence can be modified to that already undergone by the petitioner.

Accordingly, while maintaining the conviction of the petitioner- accused under Section 420 IPC, I dispose of the aforesaid revision petition by modifying the sentence to that already undergone by the petitioner.
Records be sent back to the Court concerned along with a copy of this judgment for information and compliance.

(VIKRAM AGGARWAL)
